default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is (a). きゅうそく.
default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.explanation: Meaning: “Recently, the number of foreign tourists in this town has been increasing rapidly.” / Key point: The kanji 急 has the on-reading きゅう (with a long vowel), while 速 is read そく (the reading does not undergo rendaku voicing).
default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.why.0: (a) Correct. 「急速」 consists of 急 (on-reading きゅう, with a long vowel) and 速 (on-reading そく), forming きゅうそく, meaning “rapid” or “swift.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The long vowel in the reading of 級 is missing (きゅ instead of きゅう), and the reading of 速 is incorrectly voiced (ぞく instead of そく).
default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This is a voicing trap; the kanji read そく, not ぞく.
default.q.n3-type-1-q1-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This is a long-vowel trap; the character has the long vowel う, so it is not read as the short sound きゅ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is (b). けっか.
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.explanation: Meaning: The exam results will be announced next Monday. / Key point: 促音便 occurs when つ comes before the か-row (けつ + か → けっか).
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. When 結 (けつ) combines with 果 (か), the つ changes into a geminate consonant っ, forming けっか, not けつか.
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.why.1: (b) Correct. 「結果」 consists of 結 (けつ) and 果 (か), with a sokuon sound change producing the reading けっか, meaning “result.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 結 has the unvoiced sound け, not the voiced sound げ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q2-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This is a geminate-consonant trap; the word must contain the small っ and cannot be read continuously as けか.
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is (c). しじ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.explanation: Meaning: I wrote down the instructions from the manager in my notebook. / Key point: Distinguish the voiceless/voiced sounds in 指 (し) and 示 (じ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The readings of the two kanji have been reversed; じし is the reading found in words such as 自身 and 時事.
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The character 示 in this word has the voiced reading じ, not the unvoiced reading ち.
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.why.2: (c) Correct. 「指示」 consists of 指, with the on-reading し, and 示, with the on-reading じ. It is read as しじ and means “instruction” or “direction.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q3-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both kanji are misread: the sound of 指 is incorrectly voiced as じ, and the sound of 示 is read as ち.
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is (d). おれて.
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.explanation: Meaning: Because of the strong wind, a branch in the garden broke. / Key point: The kun-reading of 折 in the intransitive verb 折れる (おれる: to break); distinguish it from other intransitive verbs such as 割れる (われる: to shatter).
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「われて」 is the te-form of the verb 割れる (to break, to crack; kanji 割).
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「はずれて」is the te-form of 外れる (to come off, be out of place, be misaligned).
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「よごれて」is the te-form of the verb 汚れる (to become dirty; 汚).
default.q.n3-type-1-q4-4.why.3: (d) Correct. 「折れて」is the te-form of the intransitive verb 折れる (to break), and 折 has the kun-reading お・れる.
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is (a). ひよう.
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.explanation: Translation: Let's calculate the cost of the trip together. / Key point: Distinguish the inner reading of 費 (ひ) from the standard on-reading of 用 (よう).
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.why.0: (a) Correct. 費用 consists of 費, with the on-reading ひ, and 用, with the on-reading よう, giving ひよう and meaning “cost” or “expense.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The kanji 費 has the on-reading ひ, not the voiced reading び (びよう is the reading of 美容 - beauty care).
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect. This is a vowel trap; the on-reading of 用 is よう, not ゆう.
default.q.n3-type-1-q5-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both the initial sound is wrong (び instead of ひ) and the following long vowel is wrong (ゆう instead of よう).
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is (b). ふくざつ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.explanation: Meaning: This machine is very complicated to use. / Key point: The on-reading of 複 (ふく) and the voiced sound in 雑 (ざつ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The kanji 雑 has the voiced on-reading ざつ (or ぞう), not the reading さつ; do not confuse it with 札 さつ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.why.1: (b) Correct. 「複雑」 consists of 複 (On-reading ふく) and 雑 (On-reading ざつ), correctly pronounced ふくざつ and meaning “complicated.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 複 is read with the short sound ふく, including く; it is not the long sound ふう.
default.q.n3-type-1-q6-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The kanji 雑 is read ざつ, not ぜつ (ぜつ is the on-reading of 絶 and 舌).
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is (c). ふせぐ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.explanation: Meaning: To prevent accidents, let's obey the traffic rules. / Key point: The kun-reading of 防 is ふせぐ; note the voiced ぐ at the end and do not confuse it with the kanji 稼 (かせぐ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「かせぐ」is the reading of the verb 稼ぐ, meaning “to earn money” or “to gain time,” because 稼 resembles 防 in its radicals and stroke structure.
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The verb ending for 防 is the voiced sound ぐ (ふせぐ), not the unvoiced く (ふせく).
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.why.2: (c) Correct. 「防ぐ」contains 防, whose kun-reading is ふせ・ぐ, and means “to prevent, ward off, or protect against.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q7-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect. This is a trap involving the initial vowel; it is read as ふ (ROOM), not お.
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is (d). じょうねつ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.explanation: Meaning: He has had a strong passion for painting since he was young. / Key point: Distinguish the voiced long-vowel reading of 情 (じょう) from the on-reading of 熱 (ねつ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This is a long-vowel trap; 情 has the long vowel う and is read as じょう, not じょ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. This is a voiced-sound trap; the kanji 情 has the voiced on-reading じょう, not the sound in しょう.
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The first kanji is missing its long vowel (じょ), and the reading of 熱 is incorrect (ち instead of つ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q8-8.why.3: (d) Correct. 「情熱」 consists of 情, with the on-reading じょう, and 熱, with the on-reading ねつ. It is read じょうねつ and means “passion, enthusiasm.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 依頼.
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: I received a work request by email.
Key point: The N3 noun 「依頼」（いらい - I-RAI）means asking someone to do something or making a request. Distinguish 依 (the person radical 亻: rely on) from 偉 (great), and 頼 (to rely on/request — the 頁 component) from 願 (wish).
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.why.0: (a) Correct. 依頼（いらい）means “request, favor, commission.” The character 依 has the 亻 radical, combined with 頼, which has the 頁 radical.
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Although 偉（as in 偉大）has the on-reading い, it does not combine with 頼 to form いらい; the correct kanji 依 has mistakenly been replaced by 偉.
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 依願 (いがん) means “according to one’s wishes or request,” as in 依願退職, and is pronounced いがん, not いらい; the character 頼 has been confused with 願.
default.q.n3-type-1-q9-9.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 偉願 is not a meaningful Japanese word; both kanji are wrong: 依 has been replaced with 偉, and 頼 with 願.
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 真似.
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: Children often imitate the way their parents speak.
Key point: The N3 noun/verb 「真似」（まね / 真似する）means to imitate or mimic. Note the written forms of 真 and 似: 真 has a horizontal stroke enclosing the inside, unlike 直; 似 combines the person radical with 以, so do not confuse it with 修, 使, or 侍.
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 直, meaning “straight” or “to fix,” may look similar to 真, but 直似 is not a Japanese vocabulary word meaning まね.
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.why.1: (b) Correct. 真似（まね）means imitation or copying someone's behavior or speech. 真 combines with 似, meaning “similar.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 直修 does not exist as a Japanese word; both 真 has been incorrectly replaced by 直 and 似 by 修.
default.q.n3-type-1-q10-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 真修 is not a word meaning “to imitate” and is not read as まね; the character 修 was mistakenly used instead of 似（亻+ 以）, confusing it with 修（亻+ 夂 + 彡）.
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 請求.
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: I was billed for the hotel room I used last month.
Key point: The N3 noun/verb 請求（せいきゅう）is commonly used when requesting payment or referring to a bill (請求書). Distinguish the 言 radical in 請 from the 氵 radical in 清, and 求 (seek/request) from 救 (save/rescue).
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 清, meaning “pure,” contains the water radical (氵) rather than the speech radical (言) found in 請; 清求 is not a meaningful word.
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Both kanji are mistaken: 請 has been changed to 清 by using the 氵radical instead of 言, and 求 has been changed to 救 by adding 攵. 清救 does not exist.
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.why.2: (c) Correct. 請求（せいきゅう） means a request for payment, a demand for money, or a claim to an entitlement. The kanji 請 combines 言 and 青, while 求 means “to demand” or “to seek.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q11-11.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The kanji 救 (as in 救助 and 救う) contains 求, but it is not used in せいきゅう; 請救 is not the correct word for billing or making a demand.
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 豊か.
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning: This town is easy to live in because it is rich in nature.
Key point: The N3 na-adjective 「豊か」（ゆたか - abundance/richness）is commonly used in expressions such as 自然が豊か (rich in nature) and 心が豊か (rich in spirit). Do not confuse 豊 with 登 (both contain 豆 at the bottom), or confuse its reading with 富 (wealth; 富む とむ).
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The lower part of 登（と in 登山, のぼる）is 豆, similar to 豊, but there is no word 「登か」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 礼（as in 礼儀 and お礼）is read れい / おれい, is not used with the okurigana か, and does not mean rich or abundant.
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 富 means “wealth” or “riches,” but with the okurigana む it forms the verb 富む (とむ), or it can be the noun 富 (とみ); it is not written as 富か for the adjective ゆたか.
default.q.n3-type-1-q12-12.why.3: (d) Correct. 豊か（ゆたか）is a na-adjective expressing abundance, richness, or prosperity (in nature, spirit, or resources). The kanji 豊 consists of 曲 above and 豆 below.
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 防ぐ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.explanation:
Meaning: To prevent catching a cold, I wore a mask when I went outside.
Key point: The N3 verb「防ぐ」（ふせぐ - prevent, ward off）describes preventing something bad from happening (風邪を防ぐ, 事故を防ぐ). Distinguish it from the four kanji sharing the 方 component but differing in their radicals: 防 (阝 radical: prevent), 妨 (女 radical: obstruct), 坊 (土 radical: boy/monk), 房 (戶 radical: room/chamber).
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 妨 (the 女 + 方 components) is used in the verb 妨げる（さまたげる: to obstruct, hinder）, and is not read ふせぐ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.why.1: (b) Correct. 防ぐ（ふせぐ）means to prevent, ward off, or protect against danger or illness. 防 consists of the 阝 radical and 方.
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 坊, consisting of the earth radical 土 and 方, is used in 赤ん坊（あかんぼう） and 坊さん（ぼうさん）; it does not combine with the okurigana ぐ to form a verb.
default.q.n3-type-1-q13-13.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 房 (the radical 戶 plus 方) appears in 冷房 (れいぼう) and 暖房 (だんぼう); it does not combine with the okurigana ぐ to form a verb.
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 比較.
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.explanation:
Translation: I tried comparing the prices and quality of the two products.
Key point: The N3 noun/verb 「比較」（ひかく / 比較する）means “comparison” or “to compare.” Distinguish 比 (to compare) from 批 (to criticize, with the hand radical 扌), and 較 (to compare, with the vehicle radical 車) from 校 (school, with the tree radical 木) and 絞 (to wring or tighten, with the silk radical 糹).
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.why.0: (a) Correct. 比較（ひかく - COMPARISON）means comparing or contrasting two or more objects. 比 (the comparison radical 比) combines with 較 (車 radical + 交) to express comparison.
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The kanji 校, with the 木 radical, is used in 学校（がっこう） and 校舎（こうしゃ）; it does not mean comparison, so 比校 is an incorrect spelling.
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The character 批 uses the hand radical (扌), as in 批判（ひはん - criticism） and 批評（ひひょう - critique）; 批較 is an incorrect form of 比.
default.q.n3-type-1-q14-14.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Both kanji are wrong: 比 has been confused with 批 (the 扌 radical), and 較 with 校 (the 木 radical). 批校 is not a meaningful word.
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is (a). サイン.
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.explanation: Translation: After checking the contents of the document again, please sign at the bottom. Knowledge point: The phrase 'サインをする' means to sign one’s name as confirmation on a document.
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.why.0: (a) Correct. サイン (sign) means “signature” or “to sign.” 「サインをする」 combines naturally with 「書類の内容を確認したら」 (“after confirming the contents of the document”).
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.why.1: (b) Incorrect. チャンス（chance）means “opportunity” and cannot be used in the context of completing paperwork.
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.why.2: (c) Incorrect. アイデア（idea）means "idea, concept," so it does not fit the meaning when placed at the bottom of the document.
default.q.n3-type-1-q15-15.why.3: (d) Incorrect. デザイン (design) means “design, style,” which does not fit the context of requesting confirmation of a document.
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 譲って.
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.explanation: Meaning: On the train, I gave my seat to an elderly person. Key expression: the idiom '席を譲る' (give up one’s seat).
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 断る（ことわる）means “to refuse” an invitation or proposal, so it does not fit the context of helping someone by giving up one's seat.
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.why.1: (b) Correct. 譲る（ゆずる）means “to give way” or “to yield.” The expression 「席を譲る」(give up one’s seat) is the standard and most appropriate phrase in the train context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 預ける（あずける） means “to deposit, entrust, or leave in someone's care,” such as money or luggage; it is not used for a seat.
default.q.n3-type-1-q16-16.why.3: (d) 拾う（ひろう）means “to pick up” an object from the ground, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 悔しい.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.explanation: Translation: We were just about to win the match, but then lost at the last moment. It's so frustrating and disappointing. Key point: The i-adjective 悔しい expresses frustration and regret after a narrow defeat.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.why.0: (a) is incorrect. 険しい（けわしい）describes rugged or steep terrain, or a stern or severe facial expression. It does not describe the emotion of failure.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 詳しい（くわしい）means “detailed” or “well-informed about” a field or topic.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.why.2: (c) Correct. 悔しい（くやしい）describes feelings of regret, frustration, or bitterness after missing a victory or getting an undesired result.
default.q.n3-type-1-q17-17.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 激しい（はげしい）means “intense” or “fierce” (as in rain, wind, or competition); it describes degree or intensity, not personal emotion.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 邪魔.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.explanation: Meaning: If you leave a large package in the middle of the room, it will get in the way, so please put it neatly in the corner. Key point: 邪魔 is a na-adjective meaning obstructive, in the way, or taking up space.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 豪華（ごうか） means 'luxurious, splendid, lavish' when describing a hotel or feast, so it does not fit the context at all.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 苦手（にがて）means poor at or not good with a subject, skill, or activity; it is not used for a physical obstacle.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 派手（はで）means flashy, gaudy, or conspicuous, usually describing clothing or style, so it does not fit luggage blocking the passage.
default.q.n3-type-1-q18-18.why.3: (d) Correct. 邪魔（じゃま）means obstructive or in the way. 「邪魔だから」 (because it is in the way) combines perfectly with 「すみに寄せてください」 (please move it to the corner).
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is (a). ぴったり.
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.explanation: Translation: These shoes fit my feet perfectly, so walking is very comfortable. Key point: The adverb 「ぴったり」 combines with the verb 合う to mean “fit perfectly” or “fit snugly.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.why.0: (a) Correct. ぴったり means “to fit exactly, perfectly.” The expression サイズにぴったり合っている is the most natural and accurate collocation for the size of clothing or shoes.
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.why.1: (b) Incorrect. ぎっしり means “packed tightly” or “filled to the brim,” commonly used for objects packed into a container or a packed schedule. It is not used to describe a good fit in size.
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.why.2: (c) Incorrect. のんびり means “leisurely” or “relaxed,” as in resting or enjoying life, and does not modify the verb 合う.
default.q.n3-type-1-q19-19.why.3: (d) Incorrect. うっかり means “carelessly” or “absentmindedly,” describing an accidental mistake, so it does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 資格.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.explanation: Translation: “In the future, I plan to obtain the necessary qualifications at university in order to become a Japanese teacher.” Key point: The expression 資格を取る means to obtain a qualification or professional certification.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 費用（ひよう）means “cost” or “expense” and commonly occurs with かかる (“cost”) or 払う (“pay”); 費用を取る is not used to mean practicing a profession.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.why.1: (b) Correct. 資格（しかく）means a qualification, certification, or professional credential. The collocation 資格を取る (obtain a qualification or certificate) is standard in educational and professional contexts.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 評判（ひょうばん）means “reputation” or “public opinion,” commonly used with 評判がいい/悪い.
default.q.n3-type-1-q20-20.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 条件（じょうけん）means “condition” and is not used in the expression “大学で条件を取る.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 問い合わせて.
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.explanation: Meaning: I tried calling the information desk to ask how to book concert tickets. Key point: The compound verb 問い合わせる (to contact someone for information) is commonly used with the particle 〜について.
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 追いかける（おいかける）means “to chase” or “to pursue” physically and has nothing to do with calling to ask for information.
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 呼び出す（よびだす）means “to call someone out” or “to summon someone to meet.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.why.2: (c) Correct. 問い合わせる（といあわせる）means “to inquire” or “to contact someone for information.” The structure 「〜について窓口に電話で問い合わせる」 (“call the information desk to inquire about something”) is completely standard.
default.q.n3-type-1-q21-21.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 申し込む（もうしこむ）means “to apply” or “to register” and usually takes a direct object with を, for example チケットを申し込む. It is not used when someone has only called to ask about how to order tickets.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 延期.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.explanation: Meaning: Tomorrow's soccer match has been postponed until next week because a typhoon is approaching. Key vocabulary: The noun '延期' means postponement or rescheduling of an event.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 節約（せつやく）means “saving” (money, electricity, water), and is not used for an event schedule.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 賛成（さんせい） means to agree with or support an opinion or proposal.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 予防（よぼう） means prevention or precaution, especially regarding illness or accidents.
default.q.n3-type-1-q22-22.why.3: (d) Correct. 延期（えんき）means “to postpone” or “to reschedule for a later time.” The structure 「来週に延期される」(be postponed to next week) is natural and accurate in the context of an event being delayed due to the weather.
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is (a). すでに.
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.explanation: Translation: By the time I arrived at the station, the last train had already left, so I could not get on. Knowledge point: The adverb 「すでに」(already) emphasizes that an event had been completed before a certain time in the past.
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.why.0: (a) Correct. すでに means "already" (similar to もう, but more formal and literary). Used with 〜出た後で, it emphasizes that the train had already left the station before the speaker arrived.
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.why.1: (b) Incorrect. まさか means “no way,” “surely not,” or “I never expected that,” and commonly occurs with speculative or negative exclamatory structures such as 〜ないだろう or 〜とは思わなかった.
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.why.2: (c) Incorrect. めったに means “rarely” and must be used with a negative ending (めったに〜ない).
default.q.n3-type-1-q23-23.why.3: (d) Incorrect. たまたま means “by chance” or “accidentally,” so it is not suitable for indicating the earlier chronological order of an action.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is (b). お詫び.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.explanation: Meaning: Because I made a serious mistake at work that caused trouble for a customer, I went with my supervisor to apologize to the customer. Key point: The formal noun お詫び means an apology or an act of making amends, and comes from the verb 詫びる.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.why.0: (a) Incorrect. お礼（おれい） means “thanks” or “a thank-you gift,” which is the complete opposite of the context of apologizing for causing trouble.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.why.1: (b) Correct. お詫び（おわび）means “an apology, an act of making amends.” When you have caused a serious problem for a customer (ミスをして迷惑をかけた), going to see the customer to apologize is expressed as 「お詫びに行く」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.why.2: (c) Incorrect. お祝い（おいわい）means "congratulations, congratulatory gift," used for happy occasions such as weddings, birthdays, and promotions.
default.q.n3-type-1-q24-24.why.3: (d) Incorrect. お見舞い（おみまい） means visiting or sending a get-well gift to someone who is ill or has had an accident. It is not used when apologizing for a work-related mistake.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 凍って.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.explanation: Translation: Because the temperature dropped to minus 5 degrees last night, the water in the pond froze. Key point: The verb '凍る' (to freeze, become frozen) describes a liquid changing state when exposed to temperatures below 0°C.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 枯れる（かれる）is used for plants such as flowers and trees that “wither” or “die,” not for pond water.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 腐る（くさる）means “to go bad, rot” (used for food and organic matter), and is unrelated to the effects of cold temperatures.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.why.2: (c) Correct. 凍る（こおる）means “to freeze” or “to become frozen.” When the temperature falls below 0 degrees (マイナス5度), saying that the pond water froze—「池の水が凍っていた」—is completely accurate.
default.q.n3-type-1-q25-25.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 濡れる（ぬれる）means “to get wet” (as with clothing or a surface covered in water); pond water itself is not described with 濡れる.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 注意しないで.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.explanation: Meaning: I was in a hurry, so I carelessly left my wallet at home. Key point: The N3 adverb 「うっかり」 describes carelessness or absentmindedness that causes an unintended mistake, equivalent to 「注意しないで」 or 「不注意で」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.why.0: (a) わざと: Incorrect. 「わざと」means “intentionally, deliberately,” which is the complete opposite of the absent-mindedness or carelessness expressed by「うっかり」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.why.1: (b) すっかり: Incorrect. 「すっかり」 means “completely, entirely” (e.g., すっかり忘れた, completely forgot), describing the degree of an action rather than a lack of attention.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.why.2: (c) 注意しないで: Correct. 「うっかり」 describes doing something carelessly or inadvertently and is synonymous with 「注意しないで」 in this context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q26-26.why.3: (d) しっかり: Incorrect. 「しっかり」 means “firmly,” “carefully,” or “seriously,” which is opposite in meaning to the absent-mindedness expressed by 「うっかり」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is (a). キャンセルしました.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.explanation: Meaning: I canceled my hotel reservation for next week. Key point: The N3 compound verb 「取り消す」 (cancel) is synonymous with the katakana verb 「キャンセルする」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.why.0: (a) キャンセルしました: Correct. 「取り消す」 means “to cancel” (a contract, reservation, appointment, etc.) and is completely synonymous with the katakana expression 「キャンセルする」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.why.1: (b) 変更（へんこう）しました: Incorrect. 「変更する」 means “to change,” such as changing a date, time, or content; it does not mean canceling something completely.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.why.2: (c) 確認（かくにん）しました: Incorrect. 「確認する」 means to check or confirm, not to cancel.
default.q.n3-type-1-q27-27.why.3: (d) 延期（えんき）しました: Incorrect. 「延期する」means “to postpone or move something to a later date,” not to cancel a transaction.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is (b). とてもよく似ています.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.explanation: Meaning: Those two people look exactly alike. Key point: The N3 vocabulary item 「そっくり」expresses an extremely high degree of similarity in appearance, voice, or other characteristics, equivalent to 「とてもよく似ている」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.why.0: (a) まったく違（ちが）います: Incorrect. 「まったく違う」means “completely different,” which is the opposite of 「そっくり」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.why.1: (b) とてもよく似（に）ています: Correct. 「そっくり」 indicates that two things have nearly identical appearances, voices, or characteristics, equivalent to 「とてもよく似ている」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.why.2: (c) とてもきれいです: Incorrect. 「とてもきれい」 means “very beautiful” and praises someone's appearance; it does not express similarity in appearance.
default.q.n3-type-1-q28-28.why.3: (d) いつも笑（わら）っています: Incorrect. 「いつも笑っている」 means “always smiling,” describing a state or action and having nothing to do with similarity.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is (d). ずっと前に.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.explanation: Meaning: If it is that package, it should have been delivered long ago. Key point: The N3 adverb 「とっくに」 (long ago) is synonymous with 「ずっと前に」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.why.0: (a) さっき: Incorrect. 「さっき」 refers to “just now” or “a short while ago,” and does not express something completed long ago like 「とっくに」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.why.1: (b) まもなく is incorrect. 「まもなく」 means “soon” or “before long,” pointing toward the near future, so it is not used for an action that was already completed in the past.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.why.2: (c) たった今: Incorrect. 「たった今」means “just now,” referring to something that happened immediately before the moment of speaking.
default.q.n3-type-1-q29-29.why.3: (d) ずっと前に is correct. 「とっくに」 is an N3 adverb indicating that something was completed or occurred a long time ago, and it is completely synonymous with 「ずっと前に」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 理由.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.explanation: Translation: "Do you know why he is angry?" Key point: The noun 「わけ」 at this level means the cause or reason for something in this context, equivalent to 「理由」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.why.0: (a) 目的（もくてき）: Incorrect. 「目的」means “purpose” or “goal,” not the reason that caused someone to become angry.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.why.1: (b) 理由（りゆう）: Correct. 「わけ」is an N3 noun expressing the cause, source, or reason for an action or emotional state, and is completely synonymous with 「理由」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.why.2: (c) 意味（いみ）: Incorrect. 「意味」 means “meaning,” as in the meaning of a word, not “reason” in this context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q30-30.why.3: (d) 意見（いけん）: Incorrect. 「意見」 means “personal opinion/viewpoint” and is not synonymous with the reason for an event.
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 書類を提出する前に、名前や住所に間違いがないか確かめてください。
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.explanation: Meaning: Check whether the name and address contain any errors before submitting the documents. Key point: The verb 「確かめる」 means to check or verify the truth or accuracy of information before taking the next action.
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「確かめる」 means “to check” or “to confirm” and is not used to mean “acknowledge or recognize someone’s efforts”; the verb 「認める」(みとめる) is required here.
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「確かめる」 is a verb and cannot modify a predicate meaning “surely” or “probably.” In this case, use the adverb 「確か」 or 「確かに」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.why.2: (c) Correct because 「確かめる」 is appropriately used to mean “check carefully to make sure there are no errors before submitting the documents.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q31-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect. To express “maintain/protect one's health,” use 「保つ」（たもつ）or 「維持（いじ）する」; it cannot be combined with 「確かめる」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 目覚まし時計が鳴らなくて寝坊したので、慌てて家を出た。
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.explanation: Meaning: Because my alarm clock did not ring, I overslept and hurriedly rushed out of the house. Key point: 「慌てる」conveys losing one's composure and acting in a flustered, frantic way when an unexpected problem occurs.
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.why.0: (a) Correct because 「慌てる」（あわてる）describes rushing or becoming flustered after suddenly losing one's composure, as when leaving home in a panic after oversleeping.
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.why.1: (b) Incorrect because reading at high speed requires the adverb 「速く」(はやく) or 「素早く」, not 「慌てて」 (“hurriedly” or “flusteredly”).
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.why.2: (c) Incorrect. To express eating quickly before the food gets cold, use 「急いで」 or 「早く」. 「慌てて」 indicates confusion or panic, not simply speed.
default.q.n3-type-1-q32-32.why.3: (d) Incorrect because “understood the answer immediately/suddenly” requires the adverb 「すぐに」 or 「急に」; the verb 「慌てて」 cannot be used with 「分かった」 in this way.
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 毎月の生活費を節約するために、食費や交際費を削ることにした。
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.explanation: Meaning: To save on monthly living expenses, I decided to cut back on food and entertainment expenses. Key point: Besides its literal meaning "to shave" or "to plane" an object, the verb 「削る」 is often used with nouns such as 費用（ひよう）, 予算（よさん）, and 時間（じかん） to mean reducing or cutting back part of something.
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.why.0: (a) Incorrect: To wipe dust off a table, use「拭く」(ふく) or「払う」, not「削る」(to shave, plane, or cut down).
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.why.1: (b) Incorrect. To erase incorrectly written characters with an eraser, use 「消す」（けす）, not 「削る」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.why.2: (c) Incorrect because using up physical strength by walking while carrying a heavy load should be expressed with 「（体力を）使う」or 「消耗（しょうもう）する」, not the collocation 「体力を削る」in this context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q33-33.why.3: (d) Correct because 「削る」（けずる）is used accurately to mean cutting back on spending or expenses.
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 先生の説明を何度も聞いたが、難しくてさっぱり分からなかった。
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.explanation: Translation: I listened to the teacher's explanation several times, but it was so difficult that I understood absolutely nothing. Key point: The adverb 「さっぱり」used with a negative form (～ない) means "not at all," describing an inability to understand, remember, or grasp something in the slightest.
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Sleeping soundly is expressed with the adverb 「ぐっすり」(「ぐっすり眠る」), not 「さっぱり」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.why.1: (b) Correct. 「さっぱり～ない」 is a fixed expression meaning “not at all...” (understand, remember, notice, and so on).
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.why.2: (c) Incorrect. For something that fits exactly, such as shoes or clothing, use the adverb 「ぴったり」, not 「さっぱり」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q34-34.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「さっぱり」 is used with negative forms; before a positive i-adjective such as 「難しい」, use 「かなり」 or 「ずいぶん」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 毎日たくさん練習したのに、最後の試合で１点差で負けて本当に悔しい。
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.explanation: Meaning: Although I practiced a lot every day, I lost the final match by only 1 point, so I felt extremely frustrated and bitterly disappointed. Key point: 「悔しい」expresses regret and frustration with oneself after failing or falling short of a goal despite making a great effort.
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.why.0: (a) Incorrect. Losing a beloved pet is a sad and heartbreaking loss, so use the adjective 「悲しい」(かなしい), not 「悔しい」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.why.1: (b) Incorrect because feeling embarrassed when many people are watching is 「恥ずかしい」（はずかしい）; 「悔しい」 describes frustration or regret after losing or failing.
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.why.2: (c) Correct. 「悔しい」（くやしい）expresses regret, frustration, or bitterness after making a great effort but narrowly losing the final match.
default.q.n3-type-1-q35-35.why.3: (d) Incorrect. After climbing a slope, use 「息が苦しい」（いきがくるしい）for being out of breath or having difficulty breathing, not 「悔しい」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.verdict: The correct answer is (a). うちに.
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.explanation: Translation: "Let's go home while it's still light outside. It will be dangerous once it gets dark." Key grammar point: 「～うちに」 (do something while the current state has not changed).
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.why.0: (a) Correct. The pattern 「A-い + うちに」means “while there is still...” or “before... changes,” describing an action taken before the current state changes (taking advantage of the fact that it is still light outside).
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「間に」indicates that one action takes place throughout the period during which another state continues; it does not convey the sense of hurrying to do something before conditions change, as 「うちに」 does.
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.why.2: (c) Incorrect.「とおりに」means “as” or “according to,” so it does not fit the meaning of this sentence.
default.q.n3-type-1-q36-1.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「たびに」means “each time” or “whenever,” which does not fit the context of urging someone to return home before dark.
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.verdict: The correct answer is (b). わりに.
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.explanation: Translation: "Although this apartment is close to the station, its rent is inexpensive and it is quiet." Key grammar point: 「～わりに（は）」 (the result is unexpected or contrary to what would normally be expected for a given standard or degree).
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「ついでに」 means “while you are at it” or “incidentally,” used when combining two actions; it does not express a comparison of degree.
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「A-い + わりに（は）」 means “although…; considering…,” expressing an evaluation that differs unexpectedly from the usual expectation. Normally, a place near a station would be expensive, but this place is cheap.
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「せいで」indicates a cause leading to a negative or undesirable result, whereas the following clause describes positive results: a low price and a quiet environment.
default.q.n3-type-1-q37-2.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「ために」indicates an ordinary purpose or cause-and-effect relationship; it does not express a contrast with a standard or expected level.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.verdict: The correct answer is (c). たびに.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.explanation: Translation: "Whenever I look at this photo, I remember the happy days of high school." Key grammar point: 「～たびに」means "every time..., always..." and describes something that happens or is felt each time.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「うちに」means “while” or “before the opportunity is lost,” and does not combine with a following clause describing a repeated psychological reflex.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ついでに」means "while doing something else, incidentally," so it does not suit a natural emotional reaction upon seeing a photograph.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.why.2: (c) Correct. The pattern 「V-る + たびに」 means “whenever…” or “every time…,” expressing that the action in the first clause is consistently followed by a similar feeling or action in the second clause.
default.q.n3-type-1-q38-3.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「とおりに」means “exactly as” or “according to,” so it does not fit the meaning or structure.
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 使うことにしている.
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.explanation: Sentence meaning: "For my health, I make it a habit to take the stairs instead of the elevator every morning." Key grammar point: 「～ことにしている」 (personally deciding to maintain a habit).
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「～ことになっている」expresses a rule, regulation, or plan established by a group or organization, not a habit set by an individual.
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「～ようになっている」describes a natural change or the operating function of a machine or system.
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「～はずになっている」is not a natural or grammatically correct Japanese pattern.
default.q.n3-type-1-q39-4.why.3: (d) Correct. The structure 「V-る + ことにしている」 expresses a habit or lifestyle rule that the speaker has personally decided on and consistently follows.
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.verdict: The correct answer is (a). おそれ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.explanation: Translation: "Because a strong typhoon is approaching, there is a risk of flooding from heavy rain tonight." Key grammar point: 「～おそれがある」(there is a risk that something bad will happen / it is feared that...).
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.why.0: (a) Correct. The structure 「Nの / V-る + おそれがある」 means “there is a risk of...” or “there is concern that...,” and is commonly used in news and forecasts to warn of potentially negative or dangerous events.
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「つもり」expresses a person’s subjective intention and is not used for natural disasters.
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「はずがある」 is not used in this structure to predict a risk; はずだ is usually used to assert a logically inferred certainty.
default.q.n3-type-1-q40-5.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「わけがある」means “there is a reason,” so it does not fit a context warning about the risk of flooding.
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.verdict: The correct answer is (b). にしたがって.
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.explanation: Translation: "The higher you climb the mountain, the more the temperature gradually drops and the colder it becomes." Key grammar point: 「～にしたがって」(as... / the more... the more..., expressing simultaneous change).
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「に対して」means “toward” or “in contrast to,” and is not used to express change in direct or inverse proportion.
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「V-る / N + にしたがって」means “as ... changes, ... also changes,” describing two processes changing in parallel, as in “the higher one goes, the lower the temperature becomes.”
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「について」 means “about” a particular topic; it does not express a change that leads to another result.
default.q.n3-type-1-q41-6.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「に関して」 means “concerning” or “regarding” and is a formal expression equivalent to について, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.verdict: The correct answer is (c). せいで.
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.explanation: Translation: "Because the bus was delayed by an accident, I was late for an important interview." Key grammar point: 「～せいで」(because of/due to... resulting in an undesirable outcome).
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「おかげで」 introduces a cause leading to a favorable result (“thanks to”); being late for an interview is an unfavorable result.
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「ついでに」 means "while you are at it" or "incidentally"; it is not used to indicate the cause of a problem.
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.why.2: (c) Correct. The pattern “plain form / Nの + せいで” means “because of / due to,” and is used for a direct cause of a negative result or an undesirable situation.
default.q.n3-type-1-q42-7.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「とおりに」means “as” or “in accordance with,” so it is not suitable for connecting a cause-and-effect clause.
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.verdict: The correct answer is (d). はずがない.
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.explanation: Translation: "Someone who trains as hard as he does every day cannot possibly lose a match so easily." Key grammar point: 「～はずがない」 (there is no way that... / surely cannot...).
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「～わけではない」means “it is not necessarily the case that…” or “it is not that…,” and is used for a partial, softened negation. It does not express an absolute negation based on clear grounds.
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「～はずである / はずだ」 means “be certain to...” or “should...,” which directly conflicts with the preceding context: after practicing hard, one cannot confidently claim that one will lose easily.
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「～ことになっている」expresses an established rule or predetermined arrangement, not a logical prediction.
default.q.n3-type-1-q43-8.why.3: (d) Correct. The pattern 「V-る + はずがない」 means “there is no way…” or “it certainly cannot be…,” expressing a strong negative belief based on reliable grounds stated in the preceding clause.
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.verdict: The correct answer is (a). とたん.
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.explanation: Sentence translation: "Because I was tired, I fell asleep immediately as soon as I lay down in bed." Key grammar point: The pattern「～たとたん（に）」(just as...; immediately after..., an unexpected event occurs).
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.why.0: (a) Correct. The pattern 「V-た + とたん（に）」 means “just as...; immediately after...,” describing the latter action as occurring almost instantaneously and naturally or unexpectedly as soon as the former action is completed.
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「間」does not directly combine with the past-tense verb in「横になった間」to describe something that happened in an instant.
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「うちに」combines with progressive, negative, or present forms to indicate a period of time; it does not combine with the past form「V-た + うち」to indicate an immediate moment.
default.q.n3-type-1-q44-9.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「ついで」means "while you're at it" and does not fit falling asleep from exhaustion.
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.verdict: The correct answer is (b). を中心に.
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.explanation: Meaning: “It has been decided that this project will be carried out with young employees at its core.” Key grammar point: 「～を中心に（して）」(with something as the center/core/focus).
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「を通して」means “through / throughout,” indicating an intermediary or a period of time; it does not identify someone or something as the central figure.
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.why.1: (b) Correct. The structure 「N + を中心に（して）」 means “centered on N” or “with N as the core,” indicating the entity that plays a key role in operating or implementing an activity.
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「に比べて」 means “compared with” and is used in comparative structures, so it does not fit the meaning here.
default.q.n3-type-1-q45-10.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「に加えて」 means “in addition to” or “not only... but also...” and does not express the core role of the young staff members.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.verdict: The correct answer is (c). にたいして.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.explanation: Meaning: “In contrast to the older brother, who is talkative and sociable, the younger brother is quiet and enjoys reading.” The key grammar point is 「～に対して」, meaning in contrast to or in opposition to another person or thing.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「にしたがって」means “as...,” “in accordance with,” or “the more...,” and is used for a process of change, not to contrast two different personalities.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.why.1: (b) Incorrect. 「に関して」means “concerning” or “regarding,” and does not express contrast.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.why.2: (c) Correct. The pattern 「plain form + なの / N + に対して」 means "in contrast to" or "as opposed to," comparing two clauses with completely contrasting characteristics.
default.q.n3-type-1-q46-11.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 「につれて」means “as something changes, something else also changes,” and is not used to indicate a contrast between two individuals.
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.verdict: The correct answer is (d). さえ.
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.explanation: Meaning: "As long as you have your passport, you can check into the hotel immediately." Key grammar point: 「～さえ～ば」 (as long as...; if only... is sufficient).
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.why.0: (a) Incorrect. 「だけ」 means “only” or “just.” When combined with a conditional form, it does not create the minimum-condition pattern expressed by 「さえ～ば」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.why.1: (b) Incorrect.「こそ」emphasizes the noun before it, meaning “precisely” or “it is because,” and is not used with「こそあれば」in this sense.
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「まで」 means “to the extent that” or “even” in an extreme, surprising sense; it does not form the conditional pattern 「さえ～ば」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q47-12.why.3: (d) Correct. The pattern 「N + さえ + V-ば」 means "as long as..." or "if only..." and indicates that meeting this minimum condition is enough for everything that follows to proceed smoothly.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.verdict: The correct answer is (b). つうじて.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.explanation: Translation: "Through volunteer activities, I made many friends and gained valuable experiences." Key point: The grammar pattern 「～を通じて」 means achieving something through a means, route, or activity.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.why.0: (a) Incorrect.「をはじめ（として）」means “beginning with,” or “ 대표ively including,” and is used to list representative examples. It does not indicate a means of obtaining an experience.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.why.1: (b) Correct. The pattern 「N + を通じて（つうじて） / を通して」 means "through N," indicating an intermediary route, means, or activity through which knowledge, relationships, or experience are gained.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 「をもとにして」means “based on” or “using as material” and is commonly used for artistic works, novels, and designs.
default.q.n3-type-1-q48-13.why.3: (d) Incorrect.「にくらべて」means “compared with” and is used for comparison; it does not fit the grammar or context.
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.verdict: The correct answer is (c). 会社を.
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.explanation:
Correct order: 2 - 1 - 3 - 4 (風邪を -> ひいたからといって -> 会社を -> 休む).
Complete sentence: 明日は大事な会議があるから、風邪をひいたからといって会社を休むわけにはいかない。
Meaning: Because there is an important meeting tomorrow, I cannot take the day off just because I have a cold.
Key grammar: V-た + からといって (just because...) combined with V-る + わけにはいかない (cannot do something due to moral responsibility or social obligations).
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 'ひいたからといって' must follow the object '風邪を' in the second position to form the conditional phrase '風邪をひいたからといって'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.why.1: (b) Incorrect because '風邪を' must come first, in position 1, as the object of the verb 'ひいた'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.why.2: (c) Correct because '会社を' is in the third position, marked by ★, and serves as the object of the verb '休む' immediately after it.
default.q.n3-type-1-q49-14.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 休む must be in the fourth position, immediately before the grammar pattern わけにはいかない.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 料理が.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.explanation:
Correct order: 4 - 3 - 2 - 1 (値段が -> 安いわりに -> 料理が -> おいしいと).
Complete sentence: このレストランは、値段が安いわりに料理がおいしいと評判だ。
Meaning: This restaurant is reputed to serve delicious food for its low prices.
Key grammar point: A-い / V-plain form + わりに（は） (although... / considering...; relatively...), expressing a result or evaluation that differs from what would normally be expected from the preceding clause.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.why.0: (a) Incorrect because おいしいと uses the quotative particle と together with 評判だ at the end of the sentence, so it must be in the fourth position.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.why.1: (b) Correct. 「料理が」 occupies the third position, marked by ★, and serves as the subject of the predicate 「おいしい」 that follows.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.why.2: (c) Incorrect because '安いわりに' must come in the second position, forming a comparison after '値段が'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q50-15.why.3: (d) Incorrect because '値段が' must come first, in position 1, to form the phrase '値段が安いわりに'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.verdict: The correct answer is (a). 楽しかった.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.explanation:
Correct order: 3 - 2 - 1 - 4 (写真を -> 見るたびに -> 楽しかった -> 高校時代を).
Complete sentence: 私はこの写真を見るたびに、楽しかった高校時代を思い出す。
Meaning: Every time I look at this photo, I remember my enjoyable high school days.
Key grammar: V-る / N + の + たびに (every time...), expressing an action or feeling that repeatedly occurs whenever something happens.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.why.0: (a) Correct because 「楽しかった」 occupies the third position (the ★ position) and modifies the noun phrase 「高校時代を」 in the fourth position.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.why.1: (b) Incorrect because '見るたびに' must be in the second position, after the verb and object 'この写真を'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.why.2: (c) Incorrect. 写真を must be in the first position, immediately after the demonstrative この in the question.
default.q.n3-type-1-q51-16.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 高校時代を must be in the fourth position, serving as the direct object of the verb 思い出す at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.verdict: The correct answer is (d). 学生証を.
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.explanation:
Correct order: 2 - 3 - 4 - 1 (本を -> 借りるときは -> 学生証を -> 見せる).
Complete sentence: この図書館では、本を借りるときは学生証を見せることになっている。
Meaning: At this library, the rule is that you must show your student ID when borrowing books.
Key grammar: V-る / V-ない + ことになっている (a rule or regulation established by a group or organization).
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the dictionary form verb 見せる comes directly before the pattern ことになっている, so it must be in the fourth position.
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.why.1: (b) Incorrect because '本を' is in position 1 and functions as the object of the verb '借りる'.
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 借りるときは must come second to form the time/condition clause 「本を借りるときは」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q52-17.why.3: (d) Correct because '学生証を' is in the third position, marked by ★, and serves as the object of the verb '見せる' in the fourth position.
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.verdict: The correct answer is (b). 強い風が.
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.explanation:
Correct word order: 4 - 3 - 2 - 1 (今夜から明日に -> かけて -> 強い風が -> 吹く).
Complete sentence: 台風が近づいているため、今夜から明日にかけて強い風が吹くおそれがある。
Meaning: Because the typhoon is approaching, there is a risk of strong winds from tonight through tomorrow.
Key grammar: N1 から N2 にかけて (from around N1 to around N2, in time or space) and V-る / N + の + おそれがある (there is a risk/fear that something undesirable may occur).
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 吹く is the dictionary-form verb that comes directly before おそれがある at the end of the sentence, so it must be in position 4.
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.why.1: (b) Correct because 「強い風が」 appears in the third position (marked ★), serving as the subject of the following predicate 「吹く」.
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.why.2: (c) Incorrect because かけて must come in the second position, following 今夜から明日に to form から〜にかけて.
default.q.n3-type-1-q53-18.why.3: (d) Incorrect. 今夜から明日に must be in the first position as the starting time for the structure.
